dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows odd and even 'transits' of very different depth and depth that changes from ~30 ppm to ~500 ppm between sectors, with a few missing transits. The flat-bottom shape, secondary dip hints and depth variability match an eclipsing binary or spot-induced dip, not a ~1 Earth-radius planet.

reasons.why: Odd and even transits differ by 4.9 sigma with 110 ppm difference (ratio 2.6) and this sign persists across sectors, the signature of an eclipsing binary at twice the folded period (25.8 d). Consistent with period_x2.

reasons.why: Depth is not steady; changes_within_a_source (SPOC p_constant=1.7553271095577706e-19, QLP p_constant=3.2553726336686486e-06) shows real variation between sectors. Several near-zero and absent transits and the huge chi2=194.4 on 6 dof indicate only a few deep dips drive the 18.69 snr signal.
reasons.value: p_constant=2.917e-39 depth_change_pct=342.5 per-sector depths 497 ppm (sector 32, SPOC), 319 ppm (sector 97, QLP) vs ~30-73 ppm in sectors 5/30 with -6 ppm in sector 31

reasons.why: Secondary at phase 0.341 is marginally above 4 sigma and sector secondary also exceeds 3 sigma in multiple sectors, with a flat-bottom (negative V) and duration matching the star. Together with odd/even and sector-depth changes this favours a blended or grazing binary whose eclipse depth and even/odd ratio vary with spot coverage/sector aperture, not a 1 Rearth planet. xgboost planet_rank=0.14 and centroid inconclusive (diff_snr 1.266/0.9625 used false) also support false positive.
